concept.name: Bullish engulfing
concept.definition: A two-candlestick pattern in which a small black (down) body is followed by a larger white (up) body whose real body completely contains the prior real body, appearing after a downtrend. Technical analysts treat it as a potential major bottom reversal signal because buyers overwhelmed the prior session's entire price range; it is an interpretive framework, not a proven predictor.
concept.intuition: After a falling session, buyers arrived with enough force to open lower and close above where the previous session opened, swallowing the sellers' progress whole.
concept.mechanics: From OHLC data: C1 < O1 (down candle), then O2 < C1 and C2 > O1, so the second real body engulfs the first. Engulfing is defined on bodies, not shadows (when the full high-low range is engulfed it is an outside bar). Confirmation is sought in follow-through buying on the next candle.
concept.formula: Bullish engulfing when C1 < O1, C2 > O2, O2 <= C1, C2 >= O1 (bodies strictly compared per convention).
concept.failure_modes: In persistent downtrends many bullish engulfing patterns mark only one-day short-covering bounces before new lows. Signals formed in choppy, range-bound markets are especially unreliable.
concept.misconceptions: The shadows do not need to be engulfed; only the real bodies matter for the classic definition. It is also not a standalone buy signal; practitioners typically demand confirmation or confluence with support.
concept.example: A stock in a downtrend closes at 48.00 after opening at 49.00; the next day it opens at 47.50 and closes at 49.50. The white body engulfs the prior black body, and traders watch for follow-through above 49.50 as confirmation.
